title: Strict-henselization stalk formula for the multiplicative sheaf
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $\mathbf G_m$ be the etale sheaf of units on $X$ [def-sc-gm-torsor], and let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $S_{(\bar x)}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $p:X\times_S S_{(\bar x)}\to X$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $q\geq0$, the canonical restriction map $(R^q f_*\mathbf G_m)_{\bar x}\to H^q((X\times_S S_{(\bar x)})_{\mathrm{Et}},p^{-1}\mathbf G_m)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Moreover the canonical map $p^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X}\to\mathbf G_{m,X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}}$ (adjoint to $\mathbf G_{m,X}\to p_*\mathbf G_{m,X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}}$, pullback of units) is an isomorphism, so that $(R^qf_*\mathbf G_m)_{\bar x}\cong H^q((X\times_SS_{(\bar x)})_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf G_m)$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), first assertion, specialized to the etale sheaf G_m; the identification p^{-1}G_m = G_m holds because X x_S S_(xbar) is the limit of the X x_S V with affine transition maps and units of a qcqs limit are the colimit of units (Tag 09YQ, lemma-directed-colimit-cohomology, with the G_m case)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unrestricted-strict-henselization-stalk] to the given quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism, the abelian etale sheaf $\mathbf G_m$, and the geometric point. This gives the canonical isomorphism $(R^qf_*\mathbf G_m)_{\bar x}\cong H^q((X\times_SS_{(\bar x)})_{\mathrm{Et}},p^{-1}\mathbf G_m)$ for every $q\geq0$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-gm-pullback-strict-henselization], the canonical map $p^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X}\to\mathbf G_{m,X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}}$ is an isomorphism. Replacing $p^{-1}\mathbf G_m$ by this canonically isomorphic units sheaf in the isomorphism of Step 1 yields the final displayed identification.
